newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-CHANG PUSHED TO THE WIRE BY PHILIPPOUSSIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG PUSHED TO THE WIRE BY PHILIPPOUSSIS.

text.p: Michael Chang was pushed to the limit by Australian Mark Philippoussis at the Paris Open on Friday before eventually winning their second round clash 7-5 3-6 7-6 and narrowly avoiding the fate of two other seeds.

Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek, the seventh seed, was knocked out 3-6 6-1 7-5 by Alberto Berasategui of Spain after waking up with stomach pains, while number 15 Jim Courier lost 6-4 7-5 to Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch.

Philippoussis, whose season had peaked with his first tournament victory in Toulouse two weeks ago, hit 25 aces to Chang's 15. He also hit the fastest serve of the Bercy tournament so far, timed at 205 kph (127 mph).
The big Australian, who turns 20 next week, gave as good as he got in the rallies, making Chang work hard for his points.
The second seeded American had looked like he would go on to win comfortably after taking the opening set with the first break of serve in the 12th game.
But it was two and a half hours later that he finally clinched the match with his third match point of the third set tiebreak which he won 9-7.
Chang now goes on to meet French Davis Cup player Boetsch who won in just over one and a half hours with a break of service in each set, the second to g 6-5 in front.
Boetsch then had to save two break points before winning on his first match point.
Number 15 seed Courier, returning after reconstruction surgery on his knee, said: "I'm missing practice. I'm half a step slower and the other players can probably sense it."
The former world number one said he was not affected by the partisan home crowd. "What you need when you're coming back are big, hostile crowds," he said.
Krajicek, suffering from the second set of his match, failed to convert two match points and did not feel well enough to attend a press conference afterwards.
The loss jeopardises Krajicek's chances of a place in the eight-man ATP Tour World Championship in Hanover next month.
There are three places still to be settled with the Bercy tournament results decisive.

Stuttgart Open winner Boris Becker, Americans Andre Agassi and Todd Martin, South African Wayne Ferreira, Chile's Marcelo Rios and Alberto Costa of Spain, all among the seeds at Bercy who had a bye in the first round, are vying for those places.
Berasategui, French Open finalist two years ago, saved two match points when he served with Krajicek leading 5-4 in the third set.
He finally won the decisive game after the fourth deuce with a fine crosscourt drive.
The Spanish world number 19 then broke Krajicek for the second time in the set to go 6-5 up and served for the match which he took on his first match point, the Dutchman hitting a baseline shot wide.
Krajicek, who made 50 unforced errors in the 86-minute match, later told organisers he woke up with stomach pains and felt them again from the second set, affecting his service.
Berasategui will meet the winner of the match between 10th seed Rios and Czech Petr Korda in the third round.
Ferreira, seeded eighth, beat Daniel Vacek of the Czech Republic 7-6 6-4.
Number 11 seed Martin, a semifinalist at Wimbledon, needed three sets to subdue Swedish qualifier Magnus Larsson 6-3 3-6 6-3 in one hour and 36 minutes.
Spaniard Felix Mantilla, the 16th seed, took three minutes less to beat Zimbabwe's Byron Black, also a qualifier, 6-1 5-7 6-2.
